R-0001 1번 · 빈칸 추론
Community gardens are often praised for producing fresh vegetables, but their influence reaches beyond food. Neighbors who rarely spoke begin exchanging seeds, tools, and advice. These repeated, low-pressure encounters gradually create trust. Thus, the greatest harvest of a community garden may be __________ rather than the crops themselves.
① higher property taxes
✓ ② stronger social connections
③ less need for public parks
④ a complete solution to hunger
⑤ competition among neighbors
▶ 해설 보기
이웃 간 반복적 교류와 신뢰 형성이 핵심이므로 stronger social connections가 정답입니다.
R-0002 2번 · 빈칸 추론
A museum replaced detailed wall labels with short questions beside its paintings. Instead of telling visitors what each work meant, the questions encouraged them to examine small details and discuss possible interpretations. Attendance remained stable, but visitors spent longer looking at individual works. The experiment suggests that effective education sometimes depends on __________ rather than supplying immediate answers.
① preventing disagreement
② reducing access to information
✓ ③ stimulating curiosity
④ requiring expert knowledge
⑤ removing every explanation
▶ 해설 보기
질문을 통해 관찰과 토론을 유도하므로 호기심 자극이 핵심입니다.
R-0003 3번 · 빈칸 추론
A river may appear unchanged from one season to the next, yet its banks are constantly reshaped by water. Tiny amounts of soil are carried away during ordinary rainfall, while sediment settles elsewhere. Over decades, these small movements can alter the river’s course. The example shows how __________ can produce major changes over time.
✓ ① gradual processes
② perfectly stable systems
③ sudden human decisions
④ unrelated accidents
⑤ short-lived fashions
▶ 해설 보기
작은 변화가 누적되어 큰 지형 변화를 만든다는 내용입니다.
R-0004 4번 · 빈칸 추론
When a company introduced flexible working hours, managers feared that employees would accomplish less without direct supervision. However, productivity rose as workers arranged demanding tasks around their periods of greatest concentration. The result challenges the assumption that effective work requires __________.
① clear goals
② regular communication
③ skilled employees
✓ ④ constant physical oversight
⑤ adequate rest
▶ 해설 보기
직접 감시 없이도 생산성이 높아졌으므로 상시 대면 감독이 필수라는 가정이 반박됩니다.
R-0005 5번 · 빈칸 추론

③ always more accurate
④ scientifically verified
⑤ impossible to challenge

② individual wealth alone

✓ ④ attitudes toward failure
⑤ students’ birth order

④ a source of rainfall
⑤ purely decorative objects

R-0322 13번 · 빈칸 추론
An air-quality laboratory installed a sensor that recorded pollution levels every minute. The new records revealed a repeated rise at dawn. At first, the team credited commuter traffic alone. The sensors had made the pattern visible, but measurements could not establish its cause without additional assumptions about the movement of air. Researchers consequently combined the readings with traffic observations and local wind models. Their investigation illustrates that abundant data become scientifically useful only when they are __________.
① collected at ever shorter intervals
✓ ② interpreted using explanations that can be tested
③ replaced by estimates based on intuition

⑤ separated from the conditions in which they were recorded

R-0324 15번 · 빈칸 추론
A crowded museum tried an unusual experiment: it removed half the objects from a popular gallery. Curators feared that visitors would leave sooner, since there was now less to see. A photographer documented a hillside each month for two decades. To a casual visitor, the landscape seemed almost identical from year to year, apart from seasonal colors. R-0334 25번 · 빈칸 추론
An astronomy department opened an online archive of telescope images to volunteers. R-0337 28번 · 빈칸 추론
A restoration team left some fallen trees in a damaged river channel. Visitors initially complained that the river looked neglected, and local officials considered removing the wood. ✓ ① the functions that apparently messy structures can provide
② the need to remove all wood from every river
③ proof that monitoring is less useful than first impressions
④ a rule that natural systems never require intervention
⑤ the importance of identical solutions for all river channels

겉보기에는 지저분한 나무가 유속 완화와 서식처 제공 등 기능을 갖는다는 점이 핵심입니다. 다만 모든 나무를 무조건 남기는 것은 아니라고 지문에서 제한합니다.
R-0520 29번 · 빈칸 추론
An archaeological team found worn steps beside a ceremonial gate. A colleague assumed the gate had been reserved for royal processions. However, the steps were too narrow for carts and carried marks from repeated foot traffic. The evidence is most consistent with the conclusion that __________.

기초 관찰: The steps were too narrow for carts and carried marks from repeated foot traffic. 초기 해석: A colleague assumed the gate had been reserved for royal processions. 따라서 The wear instead suggested that ordinary residents regularly participated in rituals. 다만 단일 사례가 모든 상황으로 일반화되는 것은 아닙니다.
R-0532 30번 · 빈칸 추론
A musician rehearsed with a metronome that gradually changed tempo. The group had mastered the piece at one fixed speed. The new evidence, however, was more informative than the original label: the shifting beat exposed moments where the ensemble relied on habit rather than listening. The difficulty is to account for both the attraction of the earlier interpretation and its failure to explain the later observation. The evidence is most consistent with the conclusion that __________. A defensible choice should explain the contrast without converting a local finding into a universal rule.
① the group had mastered the piece at one fixed speed, with no adjustment for the new evidence
② the evidence has no bearing on how the original claim should be assessed
③ the initial assumption must be rejected even in circumstances for which it was never tested
✓ ④ flexible performance requires understanding relationships beyond mechanical repetition
⑤ the shifting beat exposed moments where the ensemble relied on habit rather than listening, which proves that the same result is inevitable everywhere
▶ 해설 보기

A public park should not be evaluated solely by the number of visitors. A small neighborhood park may provide a safe meeting place for older residents, room for children to play, and shade during summer. These benefits can be substantial even when the park never becomes a tourist attraction. Measures of public value should recognize everyday social and environmental functions.

필자의 주장 (43문제)
R-0081 338번 · 필자의 주장
Schools often teach students how to find information, but they spend less time showing them how to judge its quality. A search engine can return hundreds of results without distinguishing careful research from misleading claims. Students should learn to check authorship, evidence, and publication dates before accepting online information. Critical evaluation deserves a regular place in the curriculum.
① 인터넷 검색 자체를 금지해야 한다
② 검색 결과를 무조건 신뢰해야 한다
✓ ③ 학교는 온라인 정보의 신뢰성 평가를 가르쳐야 한다
④ 모든 정보는 최신 자료만 사용해야 한다
⑤ 검색 속도를 높이는 교육이 유일한 목표다
▶ 해설 보기
검색 기술뿐 아니라 출처와 근거 평가 능력을 교육해야 합니다.
R-0082 339번 · 필자의 주장
Urban planners sometimes treat benches as minor details, yet people who walk slowly or tire easily depend on opportunities to rest. A continuous walking route without seating can exclude older residents and some people with disabilities. Cities should place accessible benches at reasonable intervals when improving pedestrian streets.
✓ ① 보행로에는 충분한 휴식 공간을 마련해야 한다
② 공공 벤치를 모두 철거해야 한다
③ 보행자는 앉지 말고 계속 이동해야 한다
④ 거리 개선에는 자동차 차선만 중요하다

R-0541 408번 · 제목 추론
An economist examined a free public transit trial. Officials had treated every extra passenger as an emissions saving. At first, that account seemed attractive: it offered a simple explanation that could be communicated without further qualification. In fact, ridership rose but many new journeys replaced walking rather than driving. The outcome provides a useful clue, but it does not establish that the same mechanism would operate under every set of conditions. The environmental effect of a policy depends on what behavior it displaces. The stronger inference is deliberately limited: it explains the observed contrast without pretending that all uncertainty has disappeared. This conclusion is not identical to the first assumption; it must account for the later observation and for the limits of the original measure. In particular, the new evidence may justify changing the interpretation without proving that the earlier account was mistaken in every conceivable setting. Consequently, the preferred interpretation should explain both the initial expectation and the evidence that complicates it, without pretending that a single example establishes a universal rule.

The first interpretation was plausible because it focused on an easily visible feature. But tagged birds provided precise paths while volunteer sightings covered a wider area. This did not make the earlier observation useless; it revealed that the original explanation had missed an important condition. Combining precision with coverage may improve a picture that neither source provides alone.
① A Familiar Prediction That Needed No Further Examination
✓ ② Beyond the First Explanation: Combining precision with coverage may improve a picture that neither source provides alone

④ When Background Details Replace All Empirical Evidence
⑤ Why a Single Indicator Is Sufficient for Every Decision

R-0661 418번 · 제목 추론
A researcher measured urban temperatures across neighboring streets. Officials relied only on the average temperature from a distant station. At first, that account seemed attractive: it offered a simple explanation that could be communicated without further qualification. In fact, tree shade produced sharp differences that a citywide average concealed. The outcome provides a useful clue, but it does not establish that the same mechanism would operate under every set of conditions. Local conditions may differ greatly from aggregate measurements. The stronger inference is deliberately limited: it explains the observed contrast without pretending that all uncertainty has disappeared. This conclusion is not identical to the first assumption; it must account for the later observation and for the limits of the original measure. In particular, the new evidence may justify changing the interpretation without proving that the earlier account was mistaken in every conceivable setting. Consequently, the preferred interpretation should explain both the initial expectation and the evidence that complicates it, without pretending that a single example establishes a universal rule.

A historian reconstructed the story of a canceled expedition. A later memoir blamed one person for the failure. At first, that account seemed attractive: it offered a simple explanation that could be communicated without further qualification. In fact, letters showed that practical delays, not a single dramatic dispute, caused the decision. The striking feature of the result was not its size but the mismatch between the expected mechanism and the one actually observed. Simple narratives can obscure the accumulation of ordinary causes. In particular, the new evidence may justify changing the interpretation without proving that the earlier account was mistaken in every conceivable setting. R-0675 502번 · 요약문 완성
A photographer removed distracting advertisements from a street scene. The original photograph was assumed to show everything equally. At first, that account seemed attractive: it offered a simple explanation that could be communicated without further qualification. In fact, viewers suddenly noticed the repetitive architecture and neglected storefronts. A quick appraisal would reward the immediately measurable result, but it could overlook the cost imposed elsewhere in the system. Attention can be directed as much by omission as by inclusion. The relevant question is whether the benefit persists once these indirect effects are included. This conclusion is not identical to the first assumption; it must account for the later observation and for the limits of the original measure. In particular, the new evidence may justify changing the interpretation without proving that the earlier account was mistaken in every conceivable setting. Consequently, the preferred interpretation should explain both the initial expectation and the evidence that complicates it, without pretending that a single example establishes a universal rule.

R-0711 505번 · 요약문 완성
A mathematician explained why a complex model required simplification. A student assumed every omitted variable made the model worthless. At first, that account seemed attractive: it offered a simple explanation that could be communicated without further qualification. In fact, some details were removed to make its central mechanisms testable. Neither the initial prediction nor the later measurement is meaningless; the mistake is to confuse either one with a complete explanation. A useful model is judged by its purpose and limits, not by completeness alone. The task is to connect the observations with the process that could plausibly have produced them. This conclusion is not identical to the first assumption; it must account for the later observation and for the limits of the original measure. In particular, the new evidence may justify changing the interpretation without proving that the earlier account was mistaken in every conceivable setting. Consequently, the preferred interpretation should explain both the initial expectation and the evidence that complicates it, without pretending that a single example establishes a universal rule.
